BiblicalUsage: Hashbadana is named once, standing beside Ezra the scribe on the pulpit of wood when the law was read to the people. He stood on Ezra's left hand with the others who upheld the reading of the law.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe standing beside Ezra on the day the law was read is honour enough: his name is on the platform where the book was opened.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
